To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KRAS mutations, BRAF mutations, and loss of PTEN expression, but not PIK3CA alterations, are independent predictors of resistance to anti-EGF therapies.

1) KRAS mutation, BRAF mutation, PIK3Cα mutation, and PTEN loss of expression are all independent predictors of resistance to anti-EGF receptor monoclonal antibodies in colorectal cancer; and 2) when expression of PTEN is considered together with mutations of KRAS and BRAF and PI3KCA, up to 75% of colorectal cancer patients unlikely to respond can be identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular determinants that may help to identify patients who are likely to respond to anti-Egfr monoclonal antibodies in the treatment of colorectal cancer.
the development of new therapies for the treatment of cancer.
the identification of molecular alterations that are predictive of response to anti-EGF monoclonal antibodies in colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a “quadruple-negative” status is a prerequisite to obtain clinical benefit with anti-EGFR antibodies in the treatment of mCRC.
the molecular alterations of the KRAS pathway are the major determinants of response to EGFR inhibitors, and that other molecular alterations are not clinically relevant.
a patient with a KRAS wild-type, BRAF wild-type, PTEN wild-type, PIK3C wild-type, CRC has a 51% chance of responding to anti-EGF monoclonal antibody therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of KRAS, PIK3, PTEN and BRAF mutations could be a good predictive biomarkers of response to anti-EGF therapies in colorectal cancer.
a multi-determinants analysis of molecular alterations in the EGFR pathway can be used to predict clinical benefit to EGFR-targetted therapies in colorectal cancer.

the presence of a single alteration in the four molecular markers analyzed (KRAS, BRAF V600E, PIK3Cα E542K/E545K, E545R, PTEN loss of expression) in colorectal cancers is a strong predictor of lack of response to anti-EGF monoclonal antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular dissection of EGFR signaling pathways is a prerequisite for the identification of CRC patients who may benefit from anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies.
the molecular characterization of CRC tumors, including KRAS, BRAFs, PIK3CAs, and PTEN, should be routinely performed to select patients for cetuxi-mab- and panitumumumab-based therapy.
the presence of any molecular alteration in the EGFR pathway, including KRAS, BRAFs, PIK3A and PTEN, should preclude the use of EGFR-targeted therapies in colorectal cancer patients.
